recipes.prompt:
Photograph a real-looking bus shelter on a dry neighbourhood street in late-morning side light. The subject is the printed advertisement mounted in the shelter's vertical panel. Use a 40 mm street-photography perspective from the pavement, only a few degrees off front-on. Frame all four edges of the panel and enough roof, bench, kerb and brickwork to make its location obvious. Let the panel take roughly two-thirds of the frame width, with the print in sharp focus. The dark metal frame is slightly scuffed at its base. The glass is clear over all lettering.

The ad is for a neighbourhood shoe repair shop. Lay it out on vivid chartreuse matte paper, using deep green ink and a bold, condensed sans-serif. Give the type wide margins and align both text groups left. Set the large headline once, following the exact line break and punctuation below.

"I CAN WALK
FROM HERE."

Leave a clear gap below the headline. Set "SHOE REPAIR" once at the bottom left in smaller capitals. Print the words and the final period without the quotation marks. The artwork consists only of these two text groups on the single flat colour. Keep the rest of the scene free of readable signs, logos and extra lettering.

On the narrow right side of the frame, a stylish adult in an ink-blue work jacket, wide slate trousers and worn leather sneakers steps away along the pavement, a burnt-orange shoulder bag swinging behind the hip. Catch a natural mid-stride, with clear dry shadows and a warm edge of sun on the jacket. Keep the person beside the panel with the entire headline and small line clear. Make the setting feel inhabited through the worn paving and the light on the brick, as in a candid photograph taken on an ordinary morning.

Deliver exactly three separate 3:2 campaign images in the order below. They follow Inès, a 28-year-old designer, during an impromptu fitting at an independent streetwear pop-up. Inès has a short blunt black bob with one apricot-coloured strand over her left brow, a silver ear cuff on her right ear, freckles across her nose and a direct gaze. She wears the same original cobalt-blue cropped jacket in every shot: matte fabric, three broad horizontal quilt channels, a visibly off-centre silver zip and plain unmarked sleeves. Keep the face, ear cuff and jacket construction consistent across all views. The styling is deliberate and current, with wide charcoal trousers and boxy white shoes, no visible branding.

1. Wide, low 24 mm shot outside the gallery. Inès steps off an orange shipping crate as if testing the jacket in motion. Photograph the full outfit in clear afternoon sun. A sharp cast shadow cuts across the pale concrete steps. Use strong geometric diagonals and plenty of room around the body.

2. Steep overhead view from above the cutting table. Inès sits on an orange stool with both forearms on the matte orange tabletop, taking a folded paper pattern out of a sleeve cuff. Put her face and the plain outer panel of her left sleeve in the same frame. Use diffuse north-window light, soft shadows and clean, readable fabric seams. This is the source image for the later sleeve edit.

3. Tight angle just below eye height at the entrance after dark. Inès glances back towards someone arriving, her face and asymmetric collar caught by direct white flash against a deep plum entrance. Keep the apricot strand, collar construction and silver cuff recognizable. Compose a confident diagonal running from the collar towards her eye.

Each result is a single complete image. Clear faces, purposeful gestures, dry surfaces and contemporary editorial finish. Keep the scene free of writing, brand marks and extra outfits.

Edit @Image1 in place. Add one small graphic motif to the visible cobalt outer panel of Inès's left sleeve. The motif consists of six pale-ivory squares in two staggered rows of three. Treat it as a matte screen print sitting inside that panel. Allow the squares to follow the existing folds, and leave a clear cobalt border between the motif and the sleeve seams, cuff and elbow.

Match the reference framing and light. Preserve Inès's face, hands and hair, the other sleeve, every seam, the silver zip, the orange table, the paper and all background details. The output should look like the same shot immediately after this one screen print was added. Keep the squares free from text or additional symbols.

Create a single 4:3 beauty editorial image in extreme close-up. An adult makeup creator applies the last of three small squared lilac decals underneath one eye before going live. Show one eye, the outer brow, the cheek, and one fingertip carefully seating the last matte square. The three squares follow the cheekbone like pixels that slipped out of a screen. A broad, precise warm-red shadow around the lash line echoes the common shape. Use an intentional off-centre composition: eye toward upper left, three crisp square edges crossing towards lower right.

Light the real skin with one neutral-white strip light from the left. A matte coral bounce lifts the far edge of the face without flattening the skin. Use a short macro focus falloff, with the eyelashes, fine skin texture, powder grains and all three decals in clear focus. Show precise line work and tiny geometric edges. Dry matte surfaces, natural skin and bold colour separation. No glamour smoothing, watermark, text, overlays or branded cosmetics.
